title: This Season on Learning How to See: The Bible
excerpt: In season 10 of Learning How to See: The Bible, Brian and co-hosts Randy and Edith Woodley explore the book of Genesis through fresh eyes.
body:
In season 10 of Learning How to See: The Bible, Brian and co-hosts Randy and Edith Woodley explore the book of Genesis through fresh eyes.

Randy Woodley, a Cherokee theologian, and Edith Woodley, a member of the Eastern Shoshone tribe, bring their own tradition and lived experience to the conversation. Randy is a Distinguished Professor of Faith and Culture at Portland Seminary, and Edith is a bead worker, seed-keeper, and storyteller. Together they lead Eloheh Indigenous Center for Earth Justice, a farm and gathering place built around the Cherokee word for harmony, abundance, wholeness, and peace.

Each episode pairs a brief reading from Genesis with an essay or story carrying similar themes. It closes with a round-table conversation about the different ways we see and experience the same stories. It's an invitation to explore some of the Bible's oldest and most familiar passages with wonder, curiosity, and room for more than one way of seeing.

New episodes are releasing weekly. The latest, "Genesis 4 — Am I My Brother's Murderer," is out today, following last week's "Genesis 1 — The Good Earth."

Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
